agent_4.question: What is the procedure for deciding whether a violating fisher forfeits a proportional portion of their catch or must take a rest day, and how is the proportional portion determined?
agent_4.answer: We decide the penalty by looking at how much a fisher went over the rule and how often they do it. 1) If a fisher’s catch is over 8 kg or if the total of all catches would exceed the 15 % lake‑stock cap, we compare the overage to the fisher’s reported catch. 2) The proportional portion forfeited is the ratio of the overage to the total catch that day. 3) If that ratio is small (less than 25 % of the allowed 8 kg or less than 2 kg overage) we simply subtract that fraction of the catch as a fine the next day. 4) If the overage is large—more than 2 kg or more than 25 % of 8 kg—or if the fisher has repeated a violation in the last three days, we require a rest day instead of a fine. 5) The rest day counts as a day when the fisher cannot fish at all, giving the lake time to recover. This keeps the penalty fair, encourages compliance, and protects the lake’s long‑term health.

For a fisher to be considered a senior in our community we’ll look at a few simple things that all of us can agree on: 1) how many years the fisher has spent on the lake, 2) how many trips they’ve taken and how often they return with a good haul, and 3) the fisher’s willingness to help others – mentoring new fishers, sharing gear, and being a voice at the community meetings. Those who have been on the lake for at least five years, regularly fish at least once a week, and have shown a history of helping others will be called seniors.

We’ll keep the chair list simple: the fisher who gets the most votes becomes chair for the following month, then that fisher steps down and the next most-voted person becomes chair. The other seniors will just sit in the council, but the chair will have the responsibility of calling the monthly meeting, keeping minutes of the pot contributions, and ensuring the funds are split fairly. The rotation keeps every senior involved, but also gives fresh ideas each month.
